### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: step 1.1
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "The scalar $c(x,t):=(1-t)+t/\lVert x\rVert_2$ is positive, since $1-t\ge0$, $t\ge0$, and $\lVert x\rVert_2>0$. [L3]"
WHY IT FAILS: this only establishes $c(x,t)\ge0$ as a sum of two nonnegative terms; it doesn't spell out why the two terms can't vanish simultaneously (they can't: $1-t=0$ forces $t=1$, at which point $t/\lVert x\rVert_2=1/\lVert x\rVert_2>0$). The claim is true and the gap is closed in well under 30 seconds.
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: note explicitly that $1-t=0$ and $t/\lVert x\rVert_2=0$ cannot both hold.
